requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I found no gaps. The `invocation` clauses are each carried out by marked code and checked by tests.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Command form and alias.** The `Command::Author` enum in `src/main.rs` declares the subject, `--config`, `--missing`, `--force`, `--stdout`, and `-v/--verbose`. It sets `alias = "author-evidence"`, and `--missing` conflicts with both `--force` and `--stdout`. It carries `{impl}` for invocation and refresh.
- **Authoring one existing subject under refresh.**
  - `main` calls `author_evidence_with_options` in `src/authoring/mod.rs`.
  - That function treats `--stdout` as `--force`, and under `--missing` it returns `None` for a current record before any configuration is resolved. `batch::subject_is_current` makes that check.
  - `AssessmentSources::prepare` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` returns a "no matching requirement or named example" error for an unknown name.
  - `AuthoringSubject::parse` also accepts `citations:` and `sites:` forms. Other requirements marked on the same code specify those, so they are not unspecified behavior.
- **Reporting subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage path.** `AuthoringOutcome` carries all of these fields. `main` formats `"{subject}: {backend} / {model}; policy …"` followed by `Evidence: …` and `Usage: …`.
- **Evidence destination.**
  - `EvidenceOutput` selects between file and stdout.
  - `configured_assessment` writes the file and returns its path, or writes the JSON to stdout and returns `None`.
  - `main` prints the path by default, or `Evidence: stdout` when there is no path.
- **Stdout mode sends the report and diagnostics to stderr.**
  - `main` uses `eprintln!` for the stdout-mode report and for the "false" diagnostic and rationale.
  - Errors propagate out of `main` to stderr.
  - The only stdout writer inside the assessment is the evidence JSON in `configured_assessment`.

**Tests**
- `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` in `tests/authoring_cli.rs` runs the `author-evidence` alias. It asserts that stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`, that `Evidence:` names `evidence/SUBJECT.json`, and that `Usage:` is present.
- `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` asserts that stdout is only the evidence JSON. It asserts that stderr holds the subject, backend, model, `Evidence: stdout`, and the usage path. It also checks the false/FIXME diagnostics and verbose behavior in stdout mode.
- `verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs` covers both `-v` and `--verbose`.
- `author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets` covers an unknown subject failing and the conflicting target flags.
- `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject` in `tests/authoring_batch.rs` covers refresh. That covers `--missing`, `--force`, `--stdout` implying `--force`, the mutual exclusion, skipping without resolving configuration, and the alias with a current record.

All of these carry `{test}` references to the requirement.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
